answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a umber as the anchor of the cost.
